correctness.rationale: For a closed set omitting u, each omitted nonleaf forces an omitted child; this gives a path to a leaf. Conversely the complement of each such path is closed and a maximal u-omitter. Finite closure systems have exactly maximal omitters as proper meet-irreducibles, giving a bijection. Each leaf contributes one path of every length up to its depth plus one. A descendant-leaf incidence count gives n <= c <= L(n-L+1) <= floor((n+1)^2/4), with equality exactly for rooted paths and optimal brooms. Executed Python checker confirmed 18,249 labelled-rooted tree instances up to n=7 and 2,238,526 candidate subsets. Computation tests finite cases only; all-size proof given in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: The full set of characteristic models is the canonical irredundant intersection representation of the Horn closure. For all rooted-tree conjunctive implication bases (unbounded premise arity, maximum occurrence-degree two), the new exact polynomial completely identifies omission-size frequencies and lets one reconstruct leaf-depth counts, while matching lower and upper extremal shapes quantify the exact representation-size range. This is a motivated complete structural classification, not an arbitrary numerical case or a generic polynomial-enumerability restatement.
